 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Elliot Anderson scored his first Premier League goal for Manchester City
 By Emlyn Begley BBC Sport journalist Elliot Anderson's fantastic volley earned Manchester City a first Premier League point in over a month as they came from behind to hold Fulham. 
 The result ended City's English record 20 consecutive wins over Fulham in all competitions, failing to beat them for the first time since 2011 - and they were booed off by their own fans.
 The in-form Cottagers led with their first shot as Oscar Bobb ran through City's defence before picking out Rodrigo Muniz, who placed his shot in the top corner.
 Erling Haaland then had a goal disallowed for City after his header was saved by Bernd Leno, who still had his hands on the ball when the striker bundled it across the line.
 In the second half, Anderson struck the equaliser with a first-time strike from outside the box after Fulham had cleared a corner.
 The midfielder was one of City's most dangerous attacking players, with Haaland's finishing not of his usual standards.
 City had more chances than Fulham - but most of the Cottagers' efforts were on target with Gianluigi Donnarumma denying Bobb, Muniz and Calvin Bassey.
 Enzo Maresca's side had lost their previous three league games, while Fulham are now unbeaten in five Premier League matches as their resurgence under Alvaro Arbeloa continues.
 What did you learn from Man City’s display? 
 Have your say on Fulham’s performance 
 Anderson steps up, Berge impresses - player ratings for Man City v Fulham 
 Published 1 hour ago 
 Man City analysis: Anderson impresses 
 Midfielder Anderson may not have had the best international break, being sent off for England against Spain, but he was so influential for City here.
 With £125m joint British record signing Enzo Fernandez on the bench, £116m Anderson started alongside the more defensively minded £86m Ayyoub Bouaddi, which enabled him to get involved at the top end of the pitch more.
 Fulham had Alex Iwobi and Shea Charles both booked for fouling Anderson - who managed four shots, the joint most of any player in the game alongside Haaland.
 His wonderful equaliser was his first Premier League goal for City and left Leno with no chance. And not long after he had a shot roll agonisingly wide of the far post from Haaland's cutback.
 But City could not find a winner - not that they were banging down the Fulham door for one - and sit in third place, five points off leaders Arsenal who face Newcastle later on Saturday.
 They will no doubt have complaints about Haaland's disallowed goal, but football's laws clearly side with Leno, who was touching the ball even if he did not have it under full control.
 Fulham analysis: Rise under Arbeloa continues 
 The writing looked like it was on the wall for former Real Madrid boss Arbeloa a few weeks into the season.
 After the exit of the long-serving Marco Silva, Fulham started slowly under the Spaniard and were bottom with two points from six games.
 But they did not lose in the following five games, which has taken them up to 14th place in the table.
 They looked far from overawed at a stadium they had not even picked up a point at in 15 years and started very brightly.
 After Muniz's fine opening goal, Bobb almost doubled their lead after nicking the ball off Nico O'Reilly - who seemed to have stopped playing for a moment - but he shot straight at Donnarumma.
 This was the first time Fulham had been ahead at half-time in a Premier League away game in 2026.
 Some may have feared the worst when Anderson levelled, but Donnarumma pulled off two saves 60 seconds apart to deny Fulham a winner - with Muniz trying to beat him at his near post and then blocking Bassey's effort with his body.
